title: A Kitchen Sponge

outline.arc: Little follows water through a sponge’s connected spaces, sees a squeeze bring it back, compares dry and damp pieces fairly, watches the sponge reopen, and keeps a question about how much it can hold.

beatIntents.intent: Establish the warm kitchen table, a fresh golden cellulose sponge, brass magnifier, tray, two clear cups, Big and Little, and a linen notebook; focus on visible pores and the opening question.
Big lowers the same sponge into a shallow dish on the tray; Little notices the wet edge creeping upward. Keep the sponge in contact with the water, with no floating drops.
Big compresses the same sponge above an empty clear cup inside the tray. Water travels down into the cup; Little watches the connection between smaller spaces and released water.

Compare two same-size pieces of the same sponge with equal small puddles and equal time, one initially dry and one damp. A split tray and small timer support the comparison; no numerical results are painted.
After the squeeze, show the released sponge fully open on the tray next to the partly filled cup. The pair notice its restored shape; depict one actual sponge, no motion duplicates.
Return to the notebook with a wordless drawing of a sponge and a clear cup; Big sits beside Little. Keep the opening water question alive with the same tray and magnifier.
